LicensePage.title: Use Supacharger with attribution, or choose a commercial license.
LicensePage.introduction: This page summarises the repository license and the licenses declared by its direct dependencies. It is a practical guide, not a substitute for the governing license texts.
LicensePage.coreBody: The repository LICENSE applies Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International to Supacharger-owned source. Attribution is required, commercial use is not permitted under that public license, and adaptations must use the same license.
LicensePage.commercialBody: A separate paid license is the route for commercial or non-attribution use. Its terms are separate from the public repository license and should be reviewed before using Supacharger in a commercial product.
LicensePage.notLegalAdvice: License summaries can omit important conditions and exceptions. Read the full texts and obtain legal advice for your use case.
LicensePage.dependenciesIntro: The installed direct runtime and development dependencies are mostly permissively licensed. These groups are based on package metadata and bundled license files in the current lockfile, not a legal opinion or a complete transitive-dependency notice.

mit.title: MIT
mit.description: Permissive licenses that generally require preservation of copyright and license notices in redistributed copies.

apache.title: Apache-2.0
apache.description: A permissive license with notice requirements and an express patent grant.

isc.title: ISC and MIT icon lineage
isc.description: Lucide declares ISC licensing and includes some Feather-derived icon work under MIT terms.

mpl.title: MPL-2.0
mpl.description: Vercel Analytics declares a file-level copyleft license. Modified covered files may carry source-availability obligations when distributed.

LicensePage.importsTitle: Does an import count as distribution?
LicensePage.importsBody: Import syntax alone does not answer that question. Client builds can copy dependency code into browser bundles, and deployments or source archives can include package files. A remotely hosted script may not be copied into Supacharger, but its service terms still apply. Compliance follows what is actually copied, modified, and distributed.
LicensePage.scopeBody: This snapshot groups declared licenses for direct packages in package.json. The lockfile also contains transitive packages, and assets, fonts, hosted services, and user-added code may have separate terms. Re-run a formal notice audit before each release.
LicensePage.auditDate: Reviewed against the repository dependency set on 22 August 2026.

faqs.question: What can I manage with Korunet?
faqs.answer: Korunet brings community conversations, direct messages, groups, events, and member discovery into one shared platform.

faqs.question: Can communities stay private?
faqs.answer: Yes. Communities can control who joins, what members can see, and which roles can organise or moderate each space.

faqs.question: Who is Korunet for?
faqs.answer: Korunet is designed for neighbourhood groups, meetups, advocacy networks, local businesses, and larger community organisations.

faqs.question: Does Korunet support multiple languages?
faqs.answer: Members can switch the interface language from the header or footer. The current demo includes English, Spanish, and Chinese.

faqs.question: How do I get started?
faqs.answer: Create an account, set up your profile, and begin with a focused group. You can add more spaces as the community grows.

LegalPage.title: Legal information
LegalPage.description: The terms and policies that govern use of Korunet and explain how personal information and cookies are handled.

sections.title: Using the service
sections.body: Use Korunet only for lawful purposes. Keep account credentials confidential, provide accurate account information, and do not interfere with the operation or security of the service.

sections.title: Your content
sections.body: You retain ownership of content you submit. You grant Korunet the permissions needed to host, display, and process that content to operate the service.

sections.title: Availability and warranties
sections.body: The service is provided as available. Features may change, be suspended, or be discontinued, and no uninterrupted or error-free operation is promised.

sections.title: Ending access
sections.body: Access may be suspended or terminated when these terms are breached, the service is misused, or continued access creates legal or security risk.

sections.title: Information collected
sections.body: Korunet may collect account details, profile information, usage data, device information, and information supplied when you contact support.

sections.title: How information is used
sections.body: Information is used to provide and secure the service, personalise the experience, communicate with users, understand product usage, and meet legal obligations.

sections.title: Sharing and retention
sections.body: Personal information is not sold. It may be shared with service providers, legal authorities when required, or other parties at your direction. Information is retained only as long as needed for these purposes.

sections.title: Your choices
sections.body: Depending on applicable law, you may request access, correction, export, or deletion of personal information and may opt out of marketing communications.

sections.title: Why cookies are used
sections.body: Cookies and similar storage can keep sessions secure, remember preferences, measure performance, and help understand how the service is used.

sections.title: Third-party services
sections.body: Providers used for authentication, payments, analytics, or embedded content may set their own cookies under their policies.

sections.title: Managing cookies
sections.body: Browser controls can block or remove cookies. Disabling essential cookies may prevent sign-in or other parts of the service from working correctly.
